title: HTAG-eNN: Hardening Technique with AND Gates for Embedded Neural Networks
problem: Embedded Neural Networks suffer from Single-Event Upsets (SEUs) that compromise reliability. Faults transitioning from 0 to 1 in network layers (except the last layer) significantly impact classification outcomes.
motivation: Ensuring reliability of neural networks in embedded systems exposed to radiation or other fault sources is critical for safety-critical applications.
method: The paper proposes HTAG, a simple hardware block that detects and mitigates SEU impact by exploiting the specific fault behavior where 0→1 transitions are the dominant failure mode in hidden layers. AND gates are used as the protection mechanism to prevent undesired bit flips from propagating through the network computation.
key_novelty: Identifying that 0→1 bit flip transitions (except in the last layer) are the dominant failure mode in embedded neural networks and designing a targeted AND-gate-based hardware protection mechanism accordingly.
contributions: Detailed analysis showing 0→1 faults (except last layer) significantly impact classification accuracy
HTAG hardware block for detecting and mitigating SEU impact with minimal overhead
Achieves 96.85% protection efficiency on LeNet-5 CNN with reduced area and critical path compared to existing approaches

metrics.area: significantly reduced overhead compared to existing approaches

limitations: The protection mechanism does not cover the classification layer; results can be improved with additional protection methods for the last layer.
